security.description: Security service — manages authentication, authorization, multi-tenant client hierarchy, user management, role-based access control, subscription plans, billing, and application access. Uses JOOQ/MySQL with a 4-level hierarchy: SYSTEM → CLIENT → CUSTOMER → CONSUMER. All IDs are ULong (unsigned 64-bit). All DTOs inherit id, createdAt, createdBy, updatedAt, updatedBy from AbstractUpdatableDTO.

applications.description: Application records in security DB. Each app belongs to one client and has an access control mode: OWN (only owning client), ANY (all clients in hierarchy), or EXPLICIT (only clients with granted access via security_app_access). Apps can have properties, dependencies on other apps, and are the root entity for roles, profiles, and permissions. Deleting via /everything removes all related UI data (pages, styles, themes, functions).

schema.appType: SecurityAppAppType enum — APP, SITE, or POSTER
schema.appAccessType: SecurityAppAppAccessType enum — OWN (default), ANY, or EXPLICIT. Controls which clients can use this app
schema.appUsageType: SecurityAppAppUsageType enum — S, B, B2C, B2B, B2X, B2B2B, B2B2C, B2B2X, B2X2C, B2X2X. Describes target audience

customEndpoints.description: Get application by code (with multi-tenant access check — verifies caller's client has access)
Grant client access to an EXPLICIT-mode application. editAccess=true allows write access
Update client's access level (read-only vs edit) for an application
Remove client access from an EXPLICIT-mode application

params.onlyWriteAccess: boolean — filter to clients with edit access only
params.name: string — filter by client name

customEndpoints.description: List clients with access to an application (paginated). Returns clients based on app's access mode
Get application property by name (e.g. custom settings, feature flags)
Create or update an application property
Delete an application property
Get application dependencies (other apps this app depends on for shared functions/schemas)
Add an application dependency
Remove an application dependency

authentication.description: Authentication and token management. Supports multiple auth methods: password, PIN, OTP, and social login (Google, Meta, Apple, Microsoft, X). The flow: credentials → validate against policy (password/OTP/PIN policy) → check failed attempts → generate JWT token. The token contains user authorities derived from: User → assigned Profiles (per app) → Roles in each Profile → Permissions in each Role. Token format is 'Authorities.APPCODE.PermissionName' for app-scoped permissions.

AuthenticationRequest.userName: string — username, email, or phone number depending on identifierType
AuthenticationRequest.otp: string — OTP code for OTP auth
AuthenticationRequest.userId: ULong — optional, for direct user auth
AuthenticationRequest.identifierType: AuthenticationIdentifierType enum — USER_NAME, PHONE_NUMBER, or EMAIL_ID (default: USER_NAME)
AuthenticationRequest.isResend: boolean — true to resend OTP (default: false)
AuthenticationRequest.cookie: boolean — return token as HTTP cookie (default: false)
AuthenticationRequest.generateOtp: boolean — generate OTP instead of authenticating (default: false)
AuthenticationRequest.ssoToken: boolean — include SSO token in response (default: false)
AuthenticationRequest.socialRegisterState: string — state token from social OAuth flow

AuthenticationResponse.verifiedAppCode: string — the app code verified during auth
AuthenticationResponse.loggedInClientCode: string — client code of the logged-in client
AuthenticationResponse.loggedInClientId: BigInteger — client ID of the logged-in client
AuthenticationResponse.managedClientCode: string — client code being managed (if acting as manager)
AuthenticationResponse.ssoToken: string — SSO token for cross-app authentication (if requested)

customEndpoints.description: Primary login endpoint. Accepts password, PIN, or OTP based on what's provided. Validates against client's auth policies, tracks failed attempts, and locks account if threshold exceeded
customEndpoints.response: AuthenticationResponse with accessToken, user, client details

customEndpoints.description: Social login callback — completes OAuth flow with Google, Meta, Apple, Microsoft, or X. Uses the socialRegisterState from the OAuth redirect

params.ssoLogout: boolean — also invalidate SSO token (default: false)

customEndpoints.description: Logout — invalidate current access token. Optionally revokes SSO token for cross-app logout
Refresh the access token using the current valid token. Returns new token with updated expiry
Verify current token is still valid and return current session info
Generate and send OTP for authentication. OTP is sent via email or SMS based on identifierType and OTP policy
Create a single-use authentication token. Used for magic links, email verification, password reset flows

users.description: User accounts within the multi-tenant system. Each user belongs to exactly one client. Users are assigned Profiles (per app) which contain Roles which contain Permissions. Permissions become 'authorities' in the JWT token. Users can have status: ACTIVE, INACTIVE, DELETED, LOCKED (auto-locked after failed auth attempts), or PASSWORD_EXPIRED. The invite flow: send invite → user receives email with code → user accepts invite with registration details → account created with pre-assigned profiles/roles.

schema.password: string — hashed password (write-only, never returned in API responses)
schema.passwordHashed: boolean — whether password is already hashed
schema.pinHashed: boolean — whether PIN is already hashed
schema.accountNonExpired: boolean — false if account has expired
schema.accountNonLocked: boolean — false if locked due to failed attempts
schema.credentialsNonExpired: boolean — false if password has expired per policy
schema.noFailedAttempt: short — count of consecutive failed password attempts
schema.noPinFailedAttempt: short — count of consecutive failed PIN attempts
schema.noOtpResendAttempts: short — count of OTP resend attempts in current session
schema.noOtpFailedAttempt: short — count of consecutive failed OTP attempts
schema.statusCode: SecurityUserStatusCode enum — ACTIVE, INACTIVE, DELETED, LOCKED, PASSWORD_EXPIRED
schema.lockedUntil: LocalDateTime — when auto-lock expires (null = indefinite lock)
schema.authorities: List<string> — computed list of permission strings (read-only)

UserInvite.profileId: ULong — profile to pre-assign on acceptance

customEndpoints.description: Assign a profile to a user. Profile must belong to an app the user has access to. User inherits all roles/permissions from the profile
Remove a profile assignment from a user. Revokes all permissions that came exclusively from that profile
Get all profiles assigned to a user for a specific app
Assign a role directly to a user (bypassing profiles). Use sparingly — profiles are the preferred assignment mechanism
Remove a direct role assignment from a user
Activate a user account (set status to ACTIVE)
Deactivate a user account (set status to INACTIVE). User can no longer log in
Unblock a user locked due to failed authentication attempts. Resets failed attempt counters and sets accountNonLocked=true
Update user's password. Validates old password, checks new password against password policy (complexity, history), hashes and stores
Send invitation email to a new user with pre-assigned profile and designation
Get invitation details by invite code — used on the acceptance page to pre-fill form

customEndpoints.body: {inviteCode: string, userName: string, password: string, firstName: string, lastName: string, phoneNumber: string}
customEndpoints.description: Accept an invitation — creates user account with pre-assigned profile/roles from the invite
Cancel/delete a pending invitation
List all pending invitations for the current client (paginated)
Check if a user exists by any identifier. Returns boolean. Used for real-time validation in registration/invite forms

params.appLevel: boolean — if true, filter by app access too

customEndpoints.description: Find all clients accessible by a user. Used when user belongs to multiple clients — shows client picker on login
Set the reporting manager for a user (for org hierarchy)
Update user's designation/title

rolev2.description: Role definitions — named groups of permissions within an application. Roles form a hierarchy: a parent role can have sub-roles. Each role contains permissions (authorities) that grant access to specific API operations. Roles are assigned to users either directly or via Profiles (preferred). The authority string format is the permission name, which becomes 'Authorities.APPCODE.PermissionName' in the JWT token for app-scoped access.

schema.appId: ULong — application this role belongs to
schema.name: string — role display name
schema.authority: string — the authority string for this role
schema.parentRoleId: ULong — parent role for hierarchy (null = top-level)
schema.permissions: List<Permission> — permissions in this role (write-only in JSON)

customEndpoints.description: Get all roles assignable within an app — combines RoleV2 records and roles from Profile assignments. Used to populate role picker dropdowns

profiles.description: Profiles — collections of roles that simplify permission assignment. Instead of assigning individual roles to users, assign a Profile that bundles multiple roles. Profiles are scoped to an application. A profile can be the 'defaultProfile' assigned automatically to new users. Profiles can be restricted to specific clients within the hierarchy. The 'arrangement' field stores UI layout preferences for the profile (e.g. sidebar structure).

schema.appId: ULong — application this profile belongs to
schema.name: string — profile name
schema.title: string — display title
schema.defaultProfile: boolean — if true, auto-assigned to new users in this app
schema.rootProfileId: ULong — ID of the root/parent profile (for profile inheritance)
schema.arrangement: Map<String, Object> — UI layout configuration (sidebar, menu structure)

customEndpoints.body: {name: string, title: string, description: string, appId: ULong, roleIds: [ULong]}
customEndpoints.description: Create a new profile with selected roles

customEndpoints.body: {id: ULong, name: string, title: string, description: string, appId: ULong, roleIds: [ULong]}
customEndpoints.description: Update a profile — can change roles, name, description
Get profile by ID with role details
Delete a profile — removes profile assignments from all users
List profiles for an application (paginated)
Restrict profile visibility to a specific client — only users of that client can be assigned this profile

clients.description: Client/tenant records in the multi-tenant hierarchy. Clients form a 4-level tree: SYSTEM (root) → CLIENT → CUSTOMER → CONSUMER. Each level inherits policies (password, OTP, PIN) from its parent unless overridden. Clients have a managerId (managing user), businessType/businessSize/industry for B2B categorization, and tokenValidityMinutes for JWT lifetime. Registration creates a new client + admin user + default plan assignment. The 'code' field is CHAR(8) max.

schema.code: string — unique client code (max 8 chars, uppercase)
schema.name: string — client display name
schema.tokenValidityMinutes: int — JWT token validity in minutes for this client's users
schema.statusCode: SecurityClientStatusCode enum — ACTIVE, INACTIVE, DELETED, LOCKED
schema.businessType: string — business type for B2B categorization
schema.levelType: SecurityClientLevelType enum — SYSTEM, CLIENT, CUSTOMER, CONSUMER. Determines position in hierarchy
schema.managerId: ULong — the user who manages this client (for client manager features)
schema.activeUsers: int — count of active users (read-only, computed)
schema.apps: List<App> — applications owned by this client (read-only)

ClientRegistrationRequest.userId: ULong — existing user ID (if linking to existing user)
ClientRegistrationRequest.passType: AuthenticationPasswordType enum — PASSWORD, PIN, or OTP
ClientRegistrationRequest.otp: string — OTP code (if passType=OTP, must be pre-verified)
ClientRegistrationRequest.socialRegisterState: string — state from social OAuth (for social-based registration)
ClientRegistrationRequest.cycleId: ULong — billing cycle of the plan
ClientRegistrationRequest.managerId: ULong — user to set as client manager

customEndpoints.description: Activate a client — sets status to ACTIVE, enables login for all its users
Deactivate a client — sets status to INACTIVE, prevents login for all its users
Register a new client with admin user. Creates: client record, admin user, client hierarchy entry, assigns default plan. Supports password/PIN/OTP and social registration
Register an existing application for a client — creates app access and assigns default profiles/roles per app registration type config

designations.description: User designations/titles within an organization. Designations form a hierarchy (parentDesignationId) and can define career progression (nextDesignationId). Each designation is scoped to a client and optionally linked to a department and a default profile (auto-assigned when user gets this designation).

schema.name: string — designation name (e.g. 'Software Engineer', 'Team Lead')
schema.parentDesignationId: ULong — parent designation in hierarchy (null = top-level)
schema.nextDesignationId: ULong — next designation in career progression
schema.profileId: ULong — default profile to assign when user gets this designation

departments.description: Organizational departments for grouping users and designations. Departments form a hierarchy (parentDepartmentId). Each department is scoped to a client.

schema.name: string — department name (e.g. 'Engineering', 'Sales')
schema.parentDepartmentId: ULong — parent department in hierarchy (null = top-level)

clientManagers.description: Client manager relationships — assigns users as managers of client tenants. Separate from the client hierarchy: a manager doesn't own the client but has delegated administrative access. Managers can view/manage the client's users, settings, and data. Used for sales teams managing customer accounts. Transfer endpoint allows reassigning clients between managers.

customEndpoints.description: Get clients managed by a specific user (paginated)
customEndpoints.response: Page<Client> — paginated list of managed clients

customEndpoints.description: Create manager relationship — assign user {uid} as manager of client {clientId}. User must belong to a parent client in the hierarchy
Transfer client management — reassign client from old manager to new manager
Remove manager relationship — user {uid} is no longer manager of client {clientId}

otp.description: OTP (One-Time Password) generation and verification. Used for: login authentication, client registration verification, password reset, and email/phone verification flows. OTP behavior is governed by the client's OTP policy (length, numeric/alphanumeric, expiry interval, max failed attempts, resend limits). OTP is sent via email or SMS based on the target type.

OtpGenerationRequest.emailId: string — recipient email (for EMAIL target type)
OtpGenerationRequest.phoneNumber: string — recipient phone (for PHONE target type)

OtpVerificationRequest.emailId: string — email used for OTP generation
OtpVerificationRequest.phoneNumber: string — phone used for OTP generation
OtpVerificationRequest.otp: string — the OTP code to verify
OtpVerificationRequest.purpose: string — must match the purpose used during generation

customEndpoints.description: Generate and send OTP to user via email or SMS. Respects client OTP policy for length, format, and expiry
Verify an OTP code. Tracks failed attempts and locks account if threshold exceeded per OTP policy

clientUrls.description: Client URL mappings — maps custom domain URLs to client+app combinations for multi-tenant routing. When a user visits a custom domain, the gateway resolves it to a specific client and app. Used for white-labeling: each client can have their own domain pointing to the same app. URLs are also linked to SSL certificates for HTTPS.

schema.clientId: ULong — client this URL belongs to
schema.appCode: string — application code this URL routes to

customEndpoints.description: Get all URLs configured for an application
Get URLs for a specific client+app combination

plans.description: Subscription plans for client billing. Plans define feature limits (users, apps, storage, etc.) and pricing via billing cycles. A plan has: cycles (billing periods with cost/tax), limits (resource caps), and can be marked for registration (shown during client signup). Plans support prepaid/postpaid models, can have a fallback plan (downgrade target), and can be scoped to a specific app or be multi-app. Each client is assigned one or more plans via the clientPlan relationship.

schema.clientId: ULong — owning client (who created the plan)
schema.name: string — plan display name
schema.fallBackPlanId: ULong — plan to downgrade to when this plan expires
schema.forRegistration: boolean — if true, shown in client registration plan picker
schema.orderNumber: int — display order in plan listings
schema.defaultPlan: boolean — if true, auto-assigned to new clients
schema.forClientId: ULong — if set, plan is restricted to this specific client
schema.appId: ULong — if set, plan is scoped to this specific app (null = multi-app plan)
schema.cycles: List<PlanCycle> — billing cycles with pricing (read-only, eager-loaded)

PlanCycle.name: string — cycle name (e.g. 'Monthly', 'Annual')
PlanCycle.cost: BigDecimal — base cost for this cycle
PlanCycle.intervalType: SecurityPlanCycleIntervalType enum — MONTH, QUARTER, ANNUAL, WEEK
PlanCycle.reminderIntervalDays: Integer — days before expiry to send renewal reminder
PlanCycle.paymentTermsDays: Integer — days after invoice to expect payment

PlanLimit.name: SecurityPlanLimitName enum — USER, CLIENT, APP, FILE, CONNECTIONS, PAGES, STORAGE, CUSTOM
PlanLimit.customName: string — display name for CUSTOM limit type

ClientPlan.nextInvoiceDate: LocalDateTime — when next invoice will be generated

Invoice._note: Auto-generated by plan billing system (no direct REST controller). Referenced by payments.
Invoice.planId: ULong — plan this invoice is for
Invoice.invoiceStatus: SecurityInvoiceInvoiceStatus enum — DRAFT, SENT, PENDING, PAID, FAILED, CANCELLED

InvoiceItem.itemTax1-5: BigDecimal — tax amounts (up to 5 tax fields)

customEndpoints.description: Get plans available for client registration — returns plans where forRegistration=true, optionally including multi-app plans
customEndpoints.response: List<Plan> with cycles and limits eager-loaded

customEndpoints.description: Assign a plan to a client — creates ClientPlan record, sets startDate and computes endDate based on cycle interval
Remove a plan from a client — deletes the ClientPlan assignment

payments.description: Payment records tracking financial transactions. Each payment is linked to an invoice and processed through a payment gateway (Stripe, Razorpay, Cashfree). The flow: invoice generated → payment initialized with gateway → user redirected to gateway → gateway callback updates payment status. Supports manual status updates for offline/manual payments.

schema.paymentStatus: SecurityPaymentPaymentStatus enum — PENDING, PAID, FAILED, CANCELLED
schema.paymentMethod: SecurityPaymentPaymentMethod enum — CASHFREE, RAZORPAY, STRIPE, OTHER
schema.paymentResponse: Map<String, Object> — raw gateway response data (for debugging/audit)

customEndpoints.body: Map<String, Object> — optional metadata for gateway
customEndpoints.description: Initialize a payment session with a gateway — creates payment record with PENDING status and returns gateway redirect/checkout info

customEndpoints.body: Map<String, Object> — raw gateway webhook payload
customEndpoints.description: Process payment gateway callback/webhook — updates payment status based on gateway response (PAID, FAILED, etc.)
Get all payment attempts for an invoice — includes successful and failed attempts
Manually update payment status — used for offline/manual payment reconciliation

paymentGateways.description: Payment gateway configurations per client. Stores encrypted credentials for external payment processors (Stripe, Razorpay, Cashfree). Each client configures their own gateway credentials so payments go to their account.

schema.clientId: ULong — client this gateway config belongs to
schema.paymentGateway: SecurityPaymentGatewayPaymentGateway enum — CASHFREE, RAZORPAY, STRIPE, OTHER
schema.paymentGatewayDetails: Map<String, Object> — encrypted gateway-specific credentials (API keys, secrets, merchant IDs)

customEndpoints.description: Get payment gateway config for a specific client and gateway type. Used during payment initialization

ssl.description: SSL certificate management for client custom domains. Supports both auto-provisioned certificates (via ACME/Let's Encrypt challenge-response) and externally issued certificates. The flow: create order request → system creates domain challenges → domain owner verifies challenges → certificate issued → certificate stored and linked to ClientUrl. Certificates auto-renew until autoRenewTill date.

schema.crtKey: string — PEM-encoded private key (write-only, never returned in API)
schema.current: Boolean — true if this is the active certificate for the URL
schema.autoRenewTill: LocalDateTime — auto-renewal cutoff date (null = no auto-renew)
schema.crtKeyUpload: string — for uploading external private key

customEndpoints.description: Create a new SSL certificate order — initiates ACME flow for domain validation

customEndpoints.body: {urlId: ULong, crt: string, crtChain: string, crtKeyUpload: string, domains: string}
customEndpoints.description: Register an externally issued SSL certificate — upload your own cert files
List SSL certificates with optional URL filter
Query SSL certificates with advanced filtering
Trigger certificate creation from a completed domain challenge
Trigger SSL domain challenge verification — checks DNS/HTTP challenge status
Get certificate request details and challenge status by URL ID
Delete a pending certificate request
Delete a certificate
Create SSL domain challenges for a request — generates DNS TXT or HTTP file challenges

transports.description: Security transport — export/import security configurations between environments (dev → staging → production). Exports a complete package of an application's security setup: roles with permissions, profiles with role assignments, app properties, and app registration configurations (access rules, role assignments, file access rules). Used for CI/CD deployment of security configurations.

TransportPOJO.name: string — transport name
TransportPOJO.uniqueTransportCode: string — unique identifier for this transport
TransportPOJO.roles: List<AppTransportRole> — roles with permissions and sub-roles
TransportPOJO.appAccess: List<AppTransportRegAppAccess> — app access registration rules by client type/level
TransportPOJO.rolesAccess: List<AppTransportRegRoles> — role registration rules by client type/level
TransportPOJO.packagesAccess: List<AppTransportRegPackages> — profile registration rules by client type/level
TransportPOJO.filesAccess: List<AppTransportRegFiles> — file access rules {resourceType, accessName, writeAccess, path, allowSubPathAccess}

customEndpoints.description: Export security transport — generates a complete TransportPOJO with all roles, profiles, properties, and registration configs for the application
Import and apply security transport — creates/updates roles, profiles, properties, and registration configs. Idempotent based on uniqueTransportCode

appRegistration.description: App registration types — configurable registration flow definitions for applications. Controls what happens when a new client registers for an app: which sub-apps get access, which roles/profiles are assigned, which departments/designations are created, and file access rules. Registrations are filtered by client level (CLIENT/CUSTOMER/CONSUMER) and business type. URL part determines the registration type: 'access' (app access), 'roles' (role assignments), 'packages' (profile assignments), 'departments', 'designations', 'fileAccess', 'profileRestriction', 'userDesignation', 'userProfile', 'userRole'.

AbstractAppRegistration (base fields).level: ClientLevelType enum — CLIENT, CUSTOMER, CONSUMER. Which hierarchy level this registration applies to

AppRegistrationAccess (urlPart: access).allowAppId: ULong — app to grant access to
AppRegistrationAccess (urlPart: access).register: boolean — also register the app for the client

customEndpoints.body: Registration type object (varies by urlPart — see schema)
customEndpoints.description: Create an app registration rule. urlPart: access, roles, packages, departments, designations, fileAccess, profileRestriction, userDesignation, userProfile, userRole

customEndpoints.body: {clientCode: string, clientId: ULong, clientType: string, level: string, businessType: string, page: int, size: int}
customEndpoints.description: Query registration rules for a specific app and type, filtered by client attributes
Delete a specific app registration rule

appRegIntegration.description: App registration social login integrations — configure OAuth2/social login providers (Google, Meta, Apple, Microsoft, X/Twitter, SSO) for application registration and login flows. Each integration stores the OAuth client credentials and endpoint URLs.

schema.platform: SecurityAppRegIntegrationPlatform enum — GOOGLE, META, APPLE, SSO, MICROSOFT, X
schema.intgId: string — OAuth client ID / integration identifier

clientOtpPolicy.description: Client OTP policies — configure OTP behavior per client and optionally per app. Policies cascade from parent client to child client in the hierarchy unless overridden. Controls: OTP length, format (numeric vs alphanumeric), expiry interval, failed attempt limits, resend limits, and user lock duration. The '/codes/policy' endpoint returns the effective policy after inheritance resolution.

schema.appId: ULong — optional app scope (write-only, null = client-wide)
schema.targetType: SecurityClientOtpPolicyTargetType enum — EMAIL, PHONE, or BOTH (default: EMAIL)
schema.isNumeric: boolean — OTP contains only digits (default: true)
schema.isAlphanumeric: boolean — OTP contains letters and digits (default: false)
schema.noFailedAttempts: short — max failed verification attempts before locking (default: 3)
schema.noResendAttempts: short — max OTP resend attempts per session (write-only, default: 3)
schema.resendSameOtp: boolean — resend the same OTP instead of generating new one (write-only)
schema.isConstant: boolean — always generate the same OTP value (write-only, for testing)
schema.constantValue: string — the constant OTP value (write-only, for testing)
schema.userLockTime: long — minutes to lock user after exceeding failed attempts (write-only, default: 15)

clientPasswordPolicy.description: Client password policies — configure password complexity and lifecycle rules per client and optionally per app. Policies cascade from parent to child client unless overridden. Controls: minimum/maximum length, character requirements (uppercase, lowercase, digit, special char), spaces, regex pattern, expiry, history (prevent reuse), and lock behavior on failed attempts.

schema.appId: ULong — optional app scope (write-only, null = client-wide)
schema.atleastOneUppercase: boolean — require at least one uppercase letter
schema.atleastOneLowercase: boolean — require at least one lowercase letter
schema.atleastOneDigit: boolean — require at least one digit
schema.atleastOneSpecialChar: boolean — require at least one special character
schema.regex: string — custom regex pattern for additional validation
schema.percentageName: short — max percentage of username allowed in password
schema.passExpiryInDays: short — password expiry in days (write-only, 0 = never expires)
schema.passExpiryWarnInDays: short — days before expiry to start warning (write-only)
schema.passHistoryCount: short — number of previous passwords to remember (write-only, prevents reuse)
schema.noFailedAttempts: short — max failed login attempts before locking (default: 3)
schema.userLockTime: long — minutes to lock user after exceeding failed attempts (write-only, default: 15)

customEndpoints.description: Get effective password policy for a client-app combination — resolves inheritance from parent client and returns the merged policy

clientPinPolicy.description: Client PIN policies — configure PIN behavior per client and optionally per app. PINs are a simpler alternative to passwords, typically 4-6 digits. Policies cascade from parent to child client. Controls: PIN length, expiry, history (prevent reuse), re-login interval (how often PIN is required), and lock behavior.

schema.appId: ULong — optional app scope (write-only, null = client-wide)
schema.reLoginAfterInterval: long — minutes after which PIN re-entry is required (write-only, default: 120)
schema.expiryInDays: short — PIN expiry in days (write-only, default: 30)
schema.expiryWarnInDays: short — days before expiry to warn (write-only, default: 25)
schema.pinHistoryCount: short — number of previous PINs to remember (write-only, default: 3)
schema.noFailedAttempts: short — max failed attempts before locking (default: 3)
schema.userLockTime: long — minutes to lock user after exceeding failed attempts (write-only, default: 15)

customEndpoints.description: Get effective PIN policy for a client-app combination — resolves inheritance from parent client and returns the merged policy
